Is there a way for current students. So, in reality, if the law schools arrange those arrangements for the current students, why should we wait 3 years. In any case, if this procedure is changed for the current students, we would have to wait 3 years for it. That is for students who joined in the first year. And we do not even know when those students will finish. Some students take even 5 years to finish a law degree programme. That is because, by failing, it drags on like this. So how will we wait for such a long period? Is there any need to necessarily wait? It is something everyone can agree is a very good thing. So if the law schools arrange this arrangement, there is no purpose at all in that waiting. Necessarily, those students, for example, have agreed; let's assume they have agreed. Even so, agreements made that way by giving an offer letter in a certain way, if any kind of regulatory change comes over it, this is not new..

Statement by the Chair:
Please keep it brief.

Statement by Ali Naeem, Vice Chair of the Legal Education Committee of the Bar Council of the Maldives:
It is not new that a regulatory change comes and affects students. The MQA has, even before this, always been proposing very many amendments on various matters. It keeps bringing amendments. Those amendments always affect students. So what happens is that, in connection with that, the obligation often lies with the colleges. In this issue too, in this matter too, the obligation lies on the colleges and institutes. Arranging those arrangements is their matter. If there is any difficulty in arranging it, they

can reach out to us as well. The Bar Council has also given that assurance of how, in what way, we can give that assistance. And in addition, a question the honourable member asked was what about students outside the Maldives. Here we have to look at why law programmes cannot be studied while in a particular place. Law programmes can be studied from anywhere. While abroad; for example, let's look! Law programmes and, for example, programmes like studying medicine are not things whose exams can be done in just any way. A medical programme cannot be studied online. In the same way, since a law programme is also very sensitive, a matter connected with the rights of very many people, in very many countries of the world, except in very few countries, a law first degree programme, a qualifying law degree that allows entry to their Bar exam, cannot be studied online. For example, in England, one of the programmes run best online is the University of London's programme. That programme is an online programme. However, even in that online programme, examinations have to be taken at some centre. For example, in the Maldives too there would be very many students studying the University of London's online programme. The arrangement for those students is made by the Department of Public Examinations, which arranges those arrangements in coordination. There will be some students; I know that sometimes, in some years, the Department of Public Examinations arranges the examination even for a single student. In the same way, for example, students are abroad. Then those institutions, even now, in very many state matters, arrange arrangements with embassies and these places. For example..

Statement by the Chair:
Please keep it a little briefer.

Statement by Ali Naeem, Vice Chairperson of the Legal Education Committee of the Bar Council:

Yes! I am wrapping up. So in this way, for example, embassies also do things like arranging signing for certain kinds of documents. If a student is abroad, there is an opportunity for that student to arrange those arrangements through embassies, or even by attending there. That is what I wanted to note.

Statement by the Chair:
I will now give the floor to Ashraf Rasheed. After that, after giving the floor to Ismail Nizar, I will give the Bar Council something to wrap up and then conclude. So I very much request that you keep it as brief as possible.

Statement by Ashraf Rasheed, Member for Faresmaathodaa constituency:
Thank you, honourable Chair. Welcome to everyone from the Bar Council. I also want to note that the amendment you have brought is in reality a good amendment. All honourable members, and you too, would bring that amendment because you yourselves believe in it. And all members accept that this is a good amendment. There is only one problem arising here. In reality, Ali Naeem has just answered the point I also wanted to clarify. So, what solution can be brought, from among this, for the students currently studying who have to bear difficulty in connection with the amendment you brought, and what can you do to bring that solution; that is all I want to clarify. Whether by talking with the Qualifications Authority, or by you talking with the colleges, what can you do to bring a solution to the problem that has arisen? Everyone accepts that some losses are happening to some people to some degree. So, what can you do to reduce that loss; that is the question I want to ask? Thank you.

Statement by the Chair:
Yes! Ismail Nizar. Then after that, by way of wrapping up, please conclude from your side with the answers to those questions together. Thank you.

Statement by Ismail Nizar, Member for North Feydhoo constituency:
Thank you, honourable Chair. Honourable member Ashraf Rasheed just asked, in sum, the question I wanted to ask. But I want to ask, do you know approximately how many students in general will be affected by bringing this regulation? I had to step out just now on a small other matter. So since I do not know the information, I just want to ask, do you know at all approximately how many students will, by estimate, be affected by this change?

Statement by Hussain Siraj, President of the Bar Council of the Maldives:
Yes! Thank you. In connection with the question you asked last. As I said earlier, at the two universities, the National University and the Islamic University, there is no such issue. That is because they always hold exams in person. Information has been shared with us by Zikura College and Villa College. Avid College has not yet shared information with us. But both Zikura College and Villa College state the total number of students currently studying. That is 161 at Zikura College. 139 at Villa College. However, these colleges have not yet shared disaggregated information with us. That is, how many students are studying in person and how many online. Thank you.

Statement by Ismail Nizar, Member for North Feydhoo constituency:
So, right [unclear]. And this is why I am saying this. I too believe that, in reality, the most important, most accurate information needed when taking a decision like this is not there.

So, as that member just noted, our request is that; we are talking about a small number of students. So we are not at all opposing this decision. When Ali Naeem just noted it, I got the answer, the answer I wanted. But doing these things through embassies, even if we say so, sometimes there are difficulties too. So our concern is that I believe a decision with such a big impact, something that brings an immediate impact on students who have been studying, should be decided only after we have talked with the institutions and settled some kind of procedure under which such matters can be arranged. That is how I see it. So, since I have no more time now, there are some questions. Even so, I will keep it short. Our request is that you look into whether a way can be found to do this with as little impact as possible on the students currently studying because of this change. That is our request. Thank you. Thank you, Chair.

Statement by the Chair:
Thank you. So, to wrap up, I give 1 minute, as the time has run out. Thank you very much for attending and participating. Yes!

Statement by Ibrahim Nazil, Member for South Hithadhoo constituency:
The President mentioned until 1 January 2027. On what basis was January set?

Statement by Hussain Siraj, President of the Bar Council of the Maldives:
1 January; excuse me, as I said earlier, we consulted stakeholders even before bringing this change. And in connection with bringing this change and announcing it, I think, before a petition came to the Majlis, since it is a procedure we made, it would first come to us. When it came, in what we discussed with the MQA and other offices, that office,

in particular a suggestion of the MQA, was to delay the implementation stage of this regulation to 1 January 2027. Thank you.

Statement by Ibrahim Shameel, Vice President of the Bar Council of the Maldives:
Yes! Thank you very much on behalf of the Bar Council for giving us the opportunity to share this information with you. The time has also run very long. I will keep it short. The summary is that the regulation we have formulated, the changes we brought, are changes we brought under the responsibility placed on the Bar Council under the Legal Profession Act, to raise the standard of the legal profession and of legal education and to ensure the integrity of the assessments made. I do not say that some students will not have to bear difficulties because of these changes. In connection with those matters, we met these students. We are meeting the law colleges. After hearing their concerns, we have now postponed the date of first implementing this amendment to 1 January 2027. When we postponed it that way, and when our relevant committees met the law colleges, they say that the main reason we postponed it to January is that, given how the colleges' studies, the stages of study, are arranged, if a semester generally starts in January, the exam for that semester will be around March or April. So, for them to arrange that arrangement from January, even though we have announced it now, if the regulation starts being applied from January, they would by then have adequate time to establish exam centres on islands and do those things. We made those decisions after taking into consideration the MQA's recommendation and those matters. Even so far, and after that too, we are addressing the complaints coming from students. As some members just noted, regarding the police service and the MNDF, places where very many students study, if concerns come to us, in coordination with those offices, to address those matters, we

can consult. There will be some matters on which we cannot take particular decisions. However, I give the assurance that, in coordination with those offices, we will give from our side the cooperation we have to give. Thank you.

Statement by the Chair:
Yes! Thank you very much. I believe very important information has been shared. So once again, on behalf of our committee, I thank the Bar Council for coming and sharing the information you have shared. And as nothing else is scheduled on today's agenda, I declare the committee meeting concluded at this point. Thank you very much. Wassalaamu alaikum.
